_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench.prepare`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.
The worked example below, machine-readable. The prose in
working_example_part1 and working_example_part2 is for the reader; this
is what a tool reads, so a visualiser runs THE EXAMPLE THIS PAGE
DESCRIBES rather than an instance somebody typed separately.
JSON inside a YAML block scalar on purpose: YAML is a superset of JSON,
so Jekyll is happy, and a reader needs no YAML parser to get at it.
`expect` is the answer this page publishes. It is what makes the
example an oracle rather than a picture: a tool can run the cascade and
check it against what the author stated, with nothing hardcoded on the
tool's side. Generation 1 pushes nothing -- every internal vertex sits
at distance 0 alongside its neighbours, so no edge is admissible.

meanings.init: Set up the starting state: no flow, no excess, every distance 0 except the source at |V|.
meanings.E01: Saturate every edge leaving the source: u = s, all destinations v.
meanings.E02: Record positive flow to the neighbours of the source, and the matching negative flow on the reverse edges.
meanings.E03: Excess at each vertex is what arrived minus what left.
meanings.E04: Build the residual graph: source edges are saturated, reverse edges back to the source open up.
meanings.E05: Mark the internal vertices — only they may hold excess.
meanings.E06: A vertex is active if it is internal and is holding excess. Computed once, to start the first round; after that the relabel step's recomputation carries it forward.
meanings.E07: Keep the residual edges (u,v) whose source u is an active vertex.
meanings.E08: An edge (u,v) is downhill when d(u) = d(v) + 1.
meanings.E09: Admissible edge (u,v): source u is active, the edge has residual capacity, and it runs downhill.
meanings.E10: Each active vertex u picks exactly one destination v to push along.
meanings.E11: Send min(excess at u, residual on (u,v)) along the chosen edge.
meanings.E12: Add the flow forward and subtract it on the reverse edge.
meanings.E13: Total flow arriving at each vertex this step.
meanings.E14: Total flow leaving each vertex this step.
meanings.E15: Excess gains what arrived and loses what left.
meanings.E16: Forward residual shrinks, reverse residual grows — this is what lets flow be undone later.
meanings.E17: Which edges are still admissible now that the push has happened — by residual and height only, at this round's heights.
meanings.E18: Does this vertex still have somewhere to push?
meanings.E19: Recompute the active set against the new excess.
meanings.E20: A vertex that still holds excess but has nowhere to push must relabel.
meanings.E21: Collect the distances of the residual neighbours v of each relabelling vertex u.
meanings.E22: The lowest neighbour distance, per relabelling vertex u.
meanings.E23: New distance for u is one above its lowest neighbour v.
meanings.E24: Apply the new distances; every other vertex keeps the one it had.
meanings.stop: No vertex is holding excess any more, so the flow is maximum.

tensorNotes.F: the flow on each edge at generation $$i$$ (the answer). $$F$$ is antisymmetric: $$F_{v,u} = -F_{u,v}$$, so a negative entry means the flow runs the other way
tensorNotes.R: the residual capacity at generation $$i$$. A saturated edge reaches $$0$$, which equals the empty value, so it simply leaves the tensor
tensorNotes.D: the distance (label) of each vertex. The empty value is not $$0$$ because $$0$$ is a legal distance
tensorNotes.Act: the active internal vertices (those holding excess)
tensorNotes.ActR: Active + Residual — Residual edges that leave an active vertex.
tensorNotes.Adm: Admissible — Admissible edges: active source, residual capacity, and downhill. Drives the push.
tensorNotes.AdmPost: Admissible, post-push — Edges still admissible after the push, by residual capacity and height alone — there is no active-vertex factor here, and the heights are still this round's, because the relabel has not happened yet. A DIFFERENT quantity from Adm, not a later generation of it: asking it after the relabel would need D_{i+1}, which needs this answer. Drives the relabel test only.
tensorNotes.FS: Flow from Source — The preflow leaving the source, before it is mirrored into the antisymmetric F.
tensorNotes.HasAdm: Has Admissible edge — Whether a vertex still has an admissible edge after the push.
tensorNotes.InPush: Inbound Push — Flow arriving at each vertex this step.
tensorNotes.Lbl: Label (distance rule) — Edges satisfying the distance rule D(u) = D(v)+1.
tensorNotes.MinNeiLbl: Minimum Neighbour Label — Lowest neighbour distance for each relabelling vertex.
tensorNotes.NST: Not Source, not Sink — Internal vertices — neither source nor sink. Only these can be active.
tensorNotes.NeiLbl: Neighbour Labels — Distances of the residual neighbours, for relabelling vertices only.
tensorNotes.NewD: New Distance — The new distance: lowest neighbour + 1.
tensorNotes.OutPush: Outbound Push — Flow leaving each vertex this step.
tensorNotes.PushCand: Push Candidate — The single edge each vertex will actually push along, chosen by the populate action.
tensorNotes.Rel: Relabel set — Vertices that must relabel: still active, nowhere to push.
tensorNotes.delta: amount pushed — Amount of flow pushed on each selected edge this step.
